clue.text: Messy hit-and-run?

parts.note: to hit someone with an open hand is to slap them
a dash is a short fast run

explanation.walkthrough: 'hit-and-run' reads as one crime, but it splits into two words joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is careless and hurried, which is to say messy.

clue.text: Deprived, due to faulty beer measure!

indicators.note: faulty means the letters of beer are out of order and must be rearranged

parts.note: FT is the abbreviation for foot or feet, a measure of length

explanation.surface: A drinker is short-changed because the beer pump measure is faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' turns BEER into BERE; add FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft means lacking or robbed of something, a close synonym of deprived.

clue.text: One US state has a right to top another

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting one piece to top another places it above, so it comes first

parts.note: another US state, here Kansas

explanation.surface: A claim that one American state has the right to lord it over another.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'to top' means A and R sit above KANSAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is a state in the southern United States.

clue.text: Disgraced bogus journalist

parts.note: something bogus is a sham, a fake
ED, short for editor, is a common crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A fraudulent reporter has been exposed and disgraced.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shamed is to be brought into disgrace or humiliation.

clue.text: US general embraced by one German girl

indicators.note: being embraced by something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ein is German for one
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: An American general is hugged by a single German girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Eileen is a woman's first name, and girls' names are fair game for 'girl'.

clue.text: Once wrong, made exact

parts.note: ex means former, so once in the sense of formerly
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Something formerly wrong has been made precise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exact' is a verb here, not the adjective it looks like; 'made' is a link: the pieces make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact payment or tribute is to demand and extract it by force, as to extort.

clue.text: They may have fallen on people's feet

definitions.text: They may have fallen on people's feet

parts.words: They may have fallen on people's feet
parts.note: the surface suggests things dropped on someone's toes

explanation.surface: Objects that have tumbled down onto someone's toes.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved structures of the foot can collapse, a condition called flat feet or fallen arches.

clue.text: Elder in sore distress

indicators.note: distress is read as a verb, damaging or upsetting the letters of in and sore into a new order

explanation.surface: An old person in painful discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is fodder: IN and SORE together give the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior is an older person, someone's elder or superior in age.

clue.text: Not a member of the first form at Westminster

definitions.text: Not a member of the first form at Westminster

parts.words: Not a member of the first form at Westminster
parts.note: the front bench seats ministers in the House of Commons; an MP without office sits behind; form also means a school class or a bench

explanation.surface: A pupil not in the first-year class at Westminster School.
explanation.walkthrough: Westminster is both a London school and the UK Parliament; a form is a school class and also a long bench.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinary MP without ministerial or shadow office sits on the rear benches of the Commons.

clue.text: Secure a basic commodity

definitions.meaning: to fasten paper together with a wire clip
a main foodstuff or product such as rice or wheat

explanation.definitionFit: Staple as a verb means fasten with wire clips; as a noun it is a staple food or main product.

clue.text: Frightening the French into preparing for war

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: arming is equipping with weapons before a war
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: France's mobilisation for war is a frightening prospect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alarming causes fear or anxiety, i.e. frightening.

clue.text: Space evolved a long time back

indicators.note: back means the letters of a and the long time are read from right to left

parts.note: an era is a long period of history

explanation.surface: Outer space came into being a very long time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses A + ERA as a whole; 'evolved' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is an expanse or region, a stretch of space.

clue.text: Agrees to a wage cut and drowns one's sorrows

definitions.meaning: accepts lower pay, a fall in income
drinks alcohol to forget troubles, has a tipple

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both accepting a reduction (in pay) and having a little alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Is unable to face the situation with free-range poultry?

definitions.text: Is unable to face the situation

definitions.meaning: hens let out of the coop, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: To back out of something through cowardice is an idiom; literally, birds allowed outdoors.

clue.text: Prime minister?

parts.note: prime means chief or principal, and a minister is a churchman; read together it suggests a head of government

explanation.definitionFit: A Roman Catholic prince of the Church is a principal clergyman, and cardinal also means chief or primary.

clue.text: Slackens off when the sun is out at quarter past eight, say

indicators.note: past means coming after, so the quarter follows the eight
the sun being out is read as its letters being out of place, so rearranged

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen; 'say' marks it as an example
S, south, is one of the four quarters or compass points

explanation.surface: Someone eases off work when the sun is shining at quarter past eight in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarter past eight' looks like a time; 'is out' rearranges SUN as UNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Unscrewing a fastening loosens it, so it slackens it off.

clue.text: Go into service?

parts.note: the services are the armed forces; the surface suggests becoming a domestic servant

explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for the armed forces, the military services.

clue.text: Make rapid progress in a profession

definitions.meaning: to rush along at speed, as a runaway vehicle does

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means hurtle along wildly; as a noun, someone's working life or occupation.

clue.text: An acrostic composed for a Latin American

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A word puzzle written in honour of someone from Latin America.
explanation.definitionFit: A Costa Rican is a native of the Central American republic, part of Latin America.

clue.text: Sums lost at rummy

indicators.note: rummy is slang for odd or strange, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Money lost while playing the card game rummy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rummy' looks like the card game, but is the old British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Totals are the results of additions, i.e. sums.

clue.text: Books with opposing points about love, in a way

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the points go round the other part

parts.note: N and S, north and south, are opposite points of the compass

indicators.note: in a way means altered in some manner, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Books that take opposing views about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges LOVE as OVEL, which N and S surround.
explanation.definitionFit: Novels are works of long fiction, a kind of book.

clue.text: Horse's blaze of celebrity

definitions.meaning: a white mark on a horse's forehead

explanation.definitionFit: A white patch on a horse's face is called this, and a famous person is also one.

clue.text: Leg side shot results in being out

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
a strike is a shot or blow at a ball

explanation.surface: A cricket stroke to the leg side gets the batsman dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface makes 'out' mean dismissed; it is the worker's out, walked out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who are out are taking industrial action, having walked off the job.

clue.text: V-sign shows one is not in agreement!

parts.note: Aries, the ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Giving a rude two-fingered gesture shows you disagree.
explanation.walkthrough: A V-sign is a rude British hand gesture; here it splits as V and a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that varies differs, so it fails to match or agree.

clue.text: Column I shall condense into a short paragraph

indicators.note: squeezing something into another piece puts it inside

parts.note: par is the short form of paragraph
I'll is the contraction of I shall

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist promises to cut a column down to a brief paragraph.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is an upright supporting post, a column in architecture.

clue.text: On which to get wind of something?

definitions.text: On which to get wind of something?

parts.words: On which to get wind of something?
parts.note: getting wind of news means hearing of it; a telephone, the old slang term, carries such news, and blowing makes wind

explanation.definitionFit: A blower is British slang for the telephone, a device on which you hear news.
